Hi Anna — pulling together the technical details you asked for. Detailed answers below; I added a KMS flow diagram for clarity.

Q: Physical residency (including backups)
A: For accounts that opt into EU-only processing we provision model-serving, KV/prefix caches, and storage volumes in EU regions (currently eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). Backups and snapshot artifacts are taken and retained in the same region and are not configured for automatic cross-region replication. We also maintain an internal flag at the account level ("eu_only=true") which prevents operator-triggered replication to non-EU zones.

Q: Lawful government access (extraterritorial requests)
A: Redwood will evaluate requests under applicable law. For EU-only accounts, we will push back on requests for production data originating from non-EU authorities and require legal process that is enforceable under EU law. We publish transparency reports for takedown and data requests on a quarterly cadence (link below). For regulatory/legal escalations we will notify the customer and provide available redacted transparency logs unless prohibited by law.

Q: KMS / key custody
A: Two modes:
- Private/Dedicated: BYOK with customer-provided HSM (PKCS#11) or KMS integration (Cloud KMS/EKM) — customer retains root key material, Redwood holds only ephemeral wrapping keys for runtime.
- Hosted (enterprise): Managed KMS with a customer-import option; keys are stored in-region and key usage logs are retained for 2 years by default (can be extended).

Q: Deletion and backups
A: Deletions follow a multi-stage workflow: 1) mark for deletion and prevent ingestion, 2) logical delete + metadata purge (24–72 hours), 3) schedule snapshot purge job; snapshot retention is configurable per account (default 30 days for hosted enterprise; 90 days for Dedicated unless overridden). On deletion we provide a purge report and a recovery-verify hash. For Private/on-prem we provide a runbook for physical media sanitization.

Q: Evidence artifacts we can provide
A: - Signed SCCs and executed DPA with subprocessors (PDF)
- KMS key metadata and key-usage logs (CSV extract)
- Account-level retention and snapshot configuration (JSON/CSV)
- Audit logs for access to storage volumes and model endpoints (redacted as needed)
- Attestation letter from our security team describing in-region processing controls

Attached: kms_keyflow-diagram.png (high-level key flow & wrapping).

Let me know if you want us to include a redactable sample of logs for your privacy team to verify patterning.

--

Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Anna — quick legal note to complement Soojin's technical detail.

1) SCCs: Redwood executes the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses with customers on enterprise contracts and maintains mapped subprocessors in the DPA appendix. Where customers require, we can provide per-subprocessor SCC addenda and are prepared to execute countersigned copies.
2) Encryption & access: We confirm data at rest and in transit are encrypted. For BYOK scenarios customers control root key material; Redwood is a custodian for wrapped keys only.
3) Evidence & attestation: We can provide a redwood-signed attestation letter summarizing the in-region controls and a signed copy of the SCCs with subprocessors. For very high assurance customers we support a short on-site or virtual attestation review with our security team.
4) Lawful requests: If we receive a non-EU lawful request for data that relates to an EU-only account we will: (a) notify the customer promptly unless prohibited, (b) require appropriate legal process that is recognized under EU law and (c) challenge requests that appear to exceed lawful scope.

DocuSign link for SCC signature: https://docusign.com/remoteSigning/abc-123-eusccs

If EuroHealth needs a written attestation tailored to your audit checklist we can produce one.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
